desc: Implement the complete final Python solution (parse rows to `cnt`, build kernel `f`, XOR-FWHT with closed-form kernel transform via Krawtchouk coefficients, pointwise multiply, inverse + scale by `1<<W`, scan min, fast I/O).

Validate edge cases and performance: `W=1` (kernel all-zero → answer 0), all-zero/all-one grids, duplicate rows aggregated via `cnt`, `H=2e5`/`W=18` handled by two slice-based FWHT passes (~2·W·2^W C-level ops); bit order irrelevant since `f` is permutation-invariant; exact division `min(p) // n` valid as transform is unnormalized.
Finalize: program reads only stdin, writes the single integer answer to stdout, no embedded sample tests, verified against sample logic (sample 1 → 2 via `c=001`, sample 2 → 0 via `c=1111`).
